title: Alcohol use disorder: severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's alcohol use, if any is reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for alcohol use.

Vitals: BP 138/84, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, BMI 28.4.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
HEENT: Negative for vision changes or ear pain.
Respiratory: Negative for cough or shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or abdominal pain.
Neurological: Negative for tremors or dizziness.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 77-year-old female presenting for ongoing management of chronic alcohol consumption. She reports regular intake of spirits throughout the week. 
[Update] The patient reports continued consumption of alcohol. She acknowledges her current drinking habits but expresses difficulty in reducing intake at this time. She denies any acute distress but remains consistent with her previous pattern of use.

Medication List:
- Multivitamin (Daily)
- Atorvastatin 20mg (Daily)

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert and oriented x3.
Psychiatric: Cooperative and engaged in conversation.
Skin: No notable rashes or lesions.
Neurological: Gait is steady; no tremors noted.

Assessment:
1. Alcohol use disorder, moderate.

Plan:
1. Discussed the risks associated with continued alcohol use.
2. Provided education on harm reduction and monitoring of consumption.
3. Patient will return in four weeks for further monitoring of alcohol use disorder, moderate.

Electronically signed, 
R. Mensah, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Alcohol use disorder, moderate or severe, indexes to alcohol dependence: F10.20 (HCC 139).

distractors.why: Moderate or severe use disorder is dependence (F10.2-); abuse has no HCC.
A use disorder with a severity is documented.

hccs.label: Alcohol Use Disorder/Moderate/Severe/Alcohol Use with Specified Non-Psychotic Complications
